ASSESSMENT CONFIRMED — action plan to lock the change

Giles has reviewed and confirmed the findings and the assumptions behind the draft scope are correct. The root cause is validated: ~65% of the procedural record is the book-in loop silently breaking (items arrive or get picked, but the Asana state is never closed out) — categories 2+3+4+1 ≈ 366 of 564 flags. And Richard's four 23.4.2026 objectives (triage dashboard, improve PICKING, mezzanine/process organisation, self-monitor metrics & report) were never closed. This plan turns that into an implementable change while Richard is away so it's ready when he returns.

CORE POSTURE — visibility + one owner first, thin checklist after. Confirmed. Do NOT hard-block completion in the first pass (C deferred); the record is a silent-break problem, and hard-blocking without proof of the QC/owner model would create false friction and train people to ignore it. We fix the 65% by making every broken loop VISIBLE daily, then add a light checklist once the overdue report proves where the loop breaks.

PHASE 1 (this week, while Richard is away) — VISIBILITY + DAILY CHASER

1. ONE Richard stock/book-in dashboard view.
   Build a Richard-specific worklist page in the OS portal (same pattern as the existing giles-worklist / andy-worklist builders already running daily via the OS Portal Status Snapshot cron). It lists every goods-in/stock-type task whose loop is NOT closed: arrived/picked but no Stock State set, overdue by delivery date, QC not ticked, or task left open. Grouped by the break type (category from the findings) so the failure mode is obvious, not a generic overdue list.

2. Auto-derive the 'broken loop' signal instead of free-text.
   Add/confirm a Stock State custom field (Arrived / Picked / Kitted / Booked-In / QC'd) and have the dashboard read it. A task is 'open loop' when it has arrived/picked status but has not reached Booked-In/Closed, or when delivery date has passed with no state change. No permission redesign needed in phase 1 — the view is read by whoever owns closure.

3. Daily per-owner overdue/chase report (Change D).
   A daily summary (morning) listing every un-closed loop with: task, age (days past delivery/arrival), current state, and which of the 9 categories it falls under. Delivery to the stock owner (Richard) + Giles. This is the self-monitor-metrics objective (his #4) made concrete.

4. Rationalise the old tag history (Change E) SO the active view is honest.
   Re-tag rather than delete: separate the 2019-2022 legacy 'Procedural Issue' flags from 2023+ so the dashboard/counts reflect recent behaviour, not 7 years of mixed history. Audit trail preserved for any HR/performance use — nothing deleted, only re-tagged/archived to a legacy bucket.

PHASE 2 (after the overdue-report has run ~2 weeks and proven where the loop breaks) — THIN CHECKLIST

5. Add a light single book-in checklist (Change A) on goods-in tasks only.
   Delivered -> QC checked -> Stock updated -> Closed. Wired as subtasks/checklist that the daily view reads; the first weeks of the phase-1 report tell us whether QC is truly a step on every goods-in or only build-critical parts, so we don't impose a wrong mandatory gate. Only after that evidence do we consider harder enforcement.

MAPPING TO RICHARD'S 4 OBJECTIVES
- Objective 1 (triage dashboard) = Phase 1 step 1 + the break-type grouping.
- Objective 2 (improve PICKING) = the Stock State field surfaces picking-stage stalls directly.
- Objective 3 (process organisation) = steps 4 + 5 (clean history + one checklist).
- Objective 4 (self-monitor metrics & report) = step 3 daily report = the concrete self-monitoring he was asked to demonstrate.

DECISIONS I NEED FROM GILES TO START PHASE 1
1. OK to build the Richard worklist page + wire it into the OS Portal daily refresh (same cron that builds giles/andy) — requires a small builder script addition.
2. Confirm the existing OS portal worklist builder is the right shell to clone for Richard's view (I believe yes — reuse, don't reinvent).
3. For step 4, confirm re-tag-not-delete on pre-2023 history is acceptable (I've assumed yes — audit trail kept).

Once Giles green-lights phase 1 I'll build steps 1-4 while Richard is away so the dashboard + daily report are live for his return. No Asana write to Richard's live tasks is needed for phase 1 — it's all read/derive + a new view + the daily report.
